title_options: Local LLM Memory: Why an 18GB Model Needs More Than 18GB
Local LLM Memory Budget: The KV Cache an 18GB Model Also Needs
Why an 18GB Local Model Does Not Fit an 18GB Budget
presentation.title_rationale: The old headline was 90 characters and read as a research summary: it opened on a jargon abbreviation (GGUF), stacked 'sizing KV cache and context' in one clause, and left the reader problem implicit. The selected 56-character title front-loads the topic (local LLM memory) and states the one benefit the page delivers - knowing that a model file is not the whole memory budget, because weights, KV cache at your num_ctx and runtime overhead are paid together (measured on qwen2.5:0.5b, computed for Qwen3-32B). Method and caveats moved to the description and introduction. The 18 GB figure is the reader's own rule of thumb; the body says no named release was verified, so the title promises no specific artifact size. It is under 80 characters, so no long_title_reason is needed.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover names the three terms the article's budget actually contains - Model weights, KV cache, Runtime overhead - so a reader who arrives believing the GGUF file is the budget sees the missing terms before reading. It is drawn only from the article's own evidence: the measured constant base (weights plus graph/allocator overhead, about 459 MiB, spread 720 KiB across contexts) and the measured slope term (KV cache, 11.98 KiB/token at f16 on qwen2.5:0.5b). Scope: conceptual checklist with no axis, no units and no drawn values, labelled 'CONCEPTUAL CHECKLIST - NOT NEW MEASUREMENT DATA' so it cannot be read as a measurement or as sizing advice for 27B-32B models.
